All around Voat, one of the major complaints about downvoats is that people use it as a "Disagree" or "I don't like you" button rather than a "This content doesn't belong here" button. So, I propose that an additional step be added to downvoating specifically: a simple "are you sure you want to downvoat?" dialogue. Human beings are impatient creatures, and the most emotional of us tend to be the least patient.

It's more than likely that people who are likely to rage or brigade against a thread will be more likely to simply browse away from a topic or block a subverse than deal with a nag screen every time they want to "dislike" a thread or OP. Meanwhile, people who are genuinely interested in actually expressing that the content isn't suited for a subverse are more likely to follow through past the nag screen. Plus, there's the added bonus of knowing that brigadiers would now have to spend twice as much energy to brigade.

Basically, it's the same concept around why large companies that depend on turnover have automated phone systems with RIDICULOUSLY deep and overly-specific selection trees. Add a time-sink to an action from which no benefit is derived for the end-user, and fewer end-users are likely to want to sink their time into that action.

Hell, even adding a CAPTCHA specifically for downvoating would probably do the trick.

IQ tests are useful for a lot of things, but they aren't the end-all, be-all measure in a person's intellectual capacity either. They measure a person's raw, natural ability to quickly think up solutions to mostly general knowledge information. It doesn't mean a lower-IQ scoring person cannot study and gain the knowledge in those subjects to meet or even exceed the knowledge in said categories a person with a higher IQ score has. IQ tests also measure specific pools of informational knowledge, they don't (and can't) literally focus on every single possible thing in existence.
